sections.title: Interview bank U08: Serving and sparse MoE

keyTerms.definition: Original practice, role-derived material. Not actual lab questions.
A set of breadth, ladder, analytical, debug, scenario, and critique questions per unit.

recall.question: What is the provenance of this interview bank?
recall.answer: Original practice, role-derived. The questions are not actual lab questions.

keyTerms.definition: The batch re-forms every iteration; removes batch-formation waiting.
Splits big prefills so decodes stop stalling.
(tokens*k/experts)*factor; overflow tokens drop.
~S each way per GPU for MoE dispatch.

recall.question: Define continuous batching. What wait does it remove?
recall.answer: The batch re-forms every iteration, admitting arrivals at once. It removes batch-formation waiting.

recall.question: Define p99 and state Little’s law. Why do means lie?
recall.answer: p99: latency 99% beat. Little: concurrency = throughput * mean latency. Means hide the tail.

recall.question: Write the expert capacity formula. What happens past capacity?
recall.answer: Capacity = (tokens*k/experts)*factor. Past capacity, tokens drop (skip the expert).

keyTerms.definition: The 0.5 s gap: not speed, pure waiting for the batch to form.
The missing mechanism when decodes stall on every new arrival.
The design experiment: replay bursty traces through both schedulers.

recall.question: Deep ladder 1 compares continuous vs static batching on 4 requests at t=0,1,2,3. What is the result?
recall.answer: Continuous mean latency 1.0 s vs static 1.5 s. Last completion ties at 4.0 s at the same token rate: the 0.5 s gap is formation waiting, not speed.

keyTerms.definition: Top-k renormalized gate outputs; the toy gives 0.646 and 0.354.
Expert 0 at 40 vs capacity 20: drops 20 (50% there).
7 of 8 experts starve: missing load-balance term.

recall.question: Deep ladder 2 routes a token through the 8-expert gate and derives capacity. What are the weights and the drop count?
recall.answer: Experts 0 and 2, weights 0.646 and 0.354. Capacity 20 at 64 tokens, top-2, factor 1.25; expert 0 getting 40 drops 20.

keyTerms.definition: Mean 1.2, p50 1.0, p99 3.0 on the 90/10 toy.
60 by Little’s law; 50 with the tail fixed.
64 MiB per step over 32 MoE layers on the toy.

recall.question: Tail: 90 requests at 1.0 s, 10 at 3.0 s. Compute mean, p50, p99, and concurrency at 50 req/s.
recall.answer: Mean 1.2, p50 1.0, p99 3.0. Concurrency 60. Tail fixed: mean 1.0, p50 1.0, p99 1.0, concurrency 50.

recall.question: Dispatch: 64 tokens, top-2, d=4096, fp16, 32 MoE layers. What is the dispatch bandwidth per GPU at 50 steps/s?
recall.answer: One way 1 MiB, round trip 2 MiB, 32 layers 64 MiB per step. At 50 steps/s: 3.2 GB/s per GPU.

keyTerms.definition: Bug class: no auxiliary balance loss.
Every expert receives a nontrivial token share each epoch.

recall.question: D1. The router trains, but 7 of 8 experts never receive tokens after the first epoch. What is the bug class, the fix, and the invariant?
recall.answer: Bug class: missing load-balance term (gate collapse). Fix: add an auxiliary balance loss to the training objective. Invariant: every expert receives a nontrivial token share each epoch.

keyTerms.definition: Dispatch free; MoE still pays gate, balance, drops, routing risk.
Bounded queue, mandatory chunking, earliest-deadline-first eviction.
Shed load early: a fast reject beats an SLO miss.

recall.question: Interconnect bandwidth is infinite. Does MoE still beat dense?
recall.answer: Dispatch is free but MoE still pays: gate compute, balance loss, capacity drops, routing quality risk. Dense wins on simplicity; MoE wins only if the extra parameters buy quality per FLOP.

recall.question: Every request has a hard 10 s SLO and arrivals are adversarial. How do you redesign admission, scheduling, eviction?
recall.answer: Bounded queue with rejection past the wait budget, prefill chunking mandatory, priority to oldest-deadline, eviction by earliest-deadline-first instead of LRU, shed load early.

keyTerms.definition: Matched quality? A weaker dense baseline invalidates.
Serving cost omitting the all-to-all invalidates.

recall.question: A paper claims “our MoE serves 8x cheaper than a dense model of equal quality.” What five audit questions do you ask?
recall.answer: (1) Matched quality? (2) Dispatch counted? (3) Utilization matched? (4) Tail SLOs? (5) Training cost counted?
